questions.question: Explain the difference between a word scale and a line scale, and why a line scale is better on a photocopied map.
questions.expected_answer: A word scale states the scale in words, e.g. 1 cm represents 5 km; a line scale is a divided bar labelled with ground distances. When a map is enlarged or reduced, the line scale changes size with the map and stays correct, but the word scale's words stay the same and become wrong.

questions.question: A map has the scale 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 7.5 cm apart. Calculate the ground distance, showing your working.
Distinguish between large-scale and small-scale maps, giving an example and a suitable use for each.
questions.expected_answer: A large-scale map shows a small area in great detail, e.g. a street map or school plan, used to find a building or plan a walk. A small-scale map shows a large area with little detail, e.g. a map of South Africa or the world, used to plan a long journey or see where countries lie.
